column1: # Branches deleted from origin on 2026-08-22, with the sha each pointed at.
# Deleting a branch does not delete its commits: `git branch <name> <sha>` or
# `git push origin <sha>:refs/heads/<name>` brings any of these back byte for byte, as long as the
# sha is written down. That is what this file is for, and it is why the cleanup was safe to do.
# Every entry was checked against `develop` by COMMIT SUBJECT, using
# `check_stranded_commits.py`'s own definition of delivered — cherry-pick and squash change sha,
# tree and patch-id, so subject is the only thing that survives delivery. Merge commits are excluded
# the same way the checker excludes them (`--no-merges`): a merge subject never survives a squash.
# Kept deliberately, NOT in this list: archive/*, backup/*, codex/checkpoint-2026-04-12,
# (the branch IS the preserved exploration), develop, master.
# Local-only tips, recorded 2026-08-22: these differed from the origin sha above,
# or the branch existed only on this machine.
# Local-only leftovers, cleared the same day after the origin sweep.
# Both `backup/*` branches pointed at EXACTLY the commits `origin/archive/*` already carries —
# the same sha under a second name, on one laptop. Removing the local name loses nothing; the
# archives on origin are the copy that matters.
# `codex/career-playbook-numeric-review` was NOT deleted. The allowlist promises it is kept "so the
# 2026-06 exploration is not lost", and it existed on one disk only — a promise a disk failure would
# have broken. It was pushed to origin instead, which is what keeping it actually means.
# Four stashes, all from June-July 2026 and all taken on branches that no longer exist, were kept as
# annotated tags and then dropped. None applied cleanly to develop in either direction any more, so
# none was restorable as a patch; the tags keep the commits themselves.
